findings.title: Loss-scaler removal deleted ClippingStats.all_finite, the only signal that clipping silently zeroes non-finite per-example gradients; the sanitization it diagnosed is unchanged and nothing replaced the signal
findings.claim: 7f55aae5 (#889) removed the data-dependent loss scaler and, in the same commit, deleted `_all_finite()`, the `aux_dict["all_finite"]` production in `clipped_fun`, the `all_finite` accumulation in `_microbatch_accumulate_stats_only`, and the public `ClippingStats.all_finite` field. The behaviour that field reported is unchanged: `clip_pytree` and `auto_scale` still begin with `tree_map(lambda t: torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0), pytree)` (_pytree.py:601 and :465), so a per-example gradient that overflows or NaNs is replaced by zeros and that record contributes nothing to the released sum. After #889 there is no signal at any layer: `ClippingStats` carries only `num_clipped`, `clipping_rate`, `batch_size`; `ClippedGradAux.grad_norms` is computed after the sanitization so a dropped record reports norm 0.0, indistinguishable from a genuinely zero gradient; and `clipping_rate` goes DOWN when records are dropped, so the failure reads as an improvement. OPQ-330 (#804) was specifically about the feedback loop `stats.all_finite -> LossScaler.update`; the fix also removed the read-only diagnostic, which was never part of the privacy defect — a statistic that is never fed back into training is not an adaptive query.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed on the current tree (repo venv, torch 2.14): fp16 params, `loss(p,x,s) = ((p['w']*x)*s).sum()`, batch rows x=[10,20,30,1000] with per-example scale s=[1,1,1,100]. Because the forward evaluates (p*x)*s, every per-example loss stays finite (`loss_values = [4.0e-3, 8.0e-3, 1.2e-2, 40.0]`, `isfinite().all() == True`) while row 4's gradient x*s = 1e5 overflows fp16 to inf. `clipped_grad(..., clipping_norm=1.0, normalize_by=4, return_aux=True)` returns `grad_norms = tensor([20., 40., 60., 0.])`, `clipped_grad_norms = tensor([0.9995, 0.9995, 0.9995, 0.0000])`; the same call with `return_stats=True` returns `ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4)`. Row 4 contributed exactly nothing and nothing in the output says so; before #889 the same `return_stats=True` call returned `all_finite=False`. Under `adaptive_clipped_grad` this compounds: the quantile tracker sees the sanitized norm 0.0 for every dropped record, so the adaptive threshold is driven down by exactly the examples that were discarded. No user-facing document states that clipping drops records this way — `grep -rn -iE 'non-finite|nonfinite|NaN/Inf|sanitiz' docs/` returns nothing and `ClippingStats`/`return_stats` appear nowhere under docs/.
evidence: git show 7f55aae5 -- packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py: deletes `def _all_finite(value)`, the field `all_finite: bool = True` with docstring "Whether every pre-clipping output in the batch was finite.", `if return_stats: aux_dict["all_finite"] = _all_finite(value)`, and the `all_finite=all_finite` accumulation in the microbatch path

executed repro output: loss_values=tensor([4.0016e-03, 8.0032e-03, 1.2001e-02, 4.0000e+01], dtype=torch.float16) True / grad_norms=tensor([20., 40., 60.,  0.]) / stats=ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4)

git show 7f55aae5 -- packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_auto.py: the AUTO-S docstring line "Its ``all_finite`` field is measured before AUTO-S sanitizes non-finite gradients" was deleted with the field, so auto_clipped_grad lost the same signal

docs/user-guide/precision.md:47-48 "Opaque therefore does not expose a loss scaler or an aggregate pre-clipping finiteness signal." and :50-51 "Low-level clipping and noise primitives still accept fp16 tensors" - the docs state the signal is gone but never state that records with non-finite gradients are dropped
grep -rn -iE 'non-finite|nonfinite|NaN/Inf|sanitiz' docs/ -> no matches; grep -rn 'ClippingStats|return_stats' docs/ -> no matches
findings.fix_sketch: Restore a read-only, non-feedback drop counter on ClippingStats (e.g. `num_nonfinite: float | dict[str, float]` computed from the same pre-clipping value `_all_finite` used) and document, in the adaptive-clipping gating style, that it must not drive any training decision. If the signal must stay removed, state explicitly in docs/user-guide/clipping.md and docs/user-guide/precision.md that per-example gradients containing NaN/Inf are replaced with zeros, that the affected records contribute nothing to the release, and that grad_norms == 0.0 is the only (ambiguous) trace.

findings.title: Bounded-Gaussian removal's replacement docs advertise float16/bfloat16 as accepted compute_dtype values on the DPTrainer surface, contradicting precision.md's explicit "do not lower" rule for the same knob
findings.claim: 873de427 (#1021) replaced the `bound` documentation on `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` with new text that presents `compute_dtype` and enumerates `float16, bfloat16, float32, float64` as accepted string names, with no caveat, in both DPTrainer-facing tables. The same commit added `_validate_compute_dtype`/`_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_DTYPES` in `_gaussian.py` and `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` in `_training_arguments.py`, both of which accept float16/bfloat16 silently (no warning, no log line). This contradicts docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70 - the page that owns this knob, rewritten by the sibling removal 7f55aae5 - which states: "Do not lower precision without a separate numerical argument. Setting compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 or torch.float16 can make the realized sensitivity and noise scale diverge from the accountant's model." A DPTrainer user reading the reference table has no prompt to consult precision.md, and the change is one config line.
findings.failure_scenario: A user sets `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={"compute_dtype": "bfloat16"}` - a value the reference table names - to cut noise-sampling memory. Verified end to end: TrainingArguments accepts it and normalizes to `{'compute_dtype': torch.bfloat16}`; _dp_trainer.py:1676-1690 forwards it verbatim into `gaussian_noise(**_gn_extra)`; _gaussian.py:190-204 then computes `center_c = center.to(torch.bfloat16)` and `sample = center_c + std * noise` entirely in bfloat16, so the released vector's pre-noise component is a bfloat16 rounding of the clipped sum and its norm can exceed the accounted clip norm. Measured over 200 draws of a 4096-dim gradient placed exactly on the clip sphere (C=1.0, noise_multiplier=1e-8): worst realized norm 1.0001227260086283 under compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 (relative excess 1.23e-4) versus 1.0000001791386004 under torch.float32 (1.79e-7) - the realized sensitivity exceeds the C the accountant is calibrated to by roughly 700x more margin. Separately the noise becomes coarsely discretized: 200000 draws at nm=1.0 gave 2945 distinct values under bfloat16 versus 199721 under float32, so the released mechanism is a coarse discrete approximation of the continuous Gaussian the PLD assumes. Neither effect produces any warning. The measured sensitivity inflation is small (1.2e-4 relative); the discretization effect was not converted into an epsilon delta and would need a floating-point-DP analysis (Mironov 2012) to bound.
evidence: git show 873de427 -- docs/reference/transformers.md: `-| privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs | ... | Forwarded into the noise mechanism factory (e.g. bound for bounded Gaussian). |` replaced by `+| ... | Gaussian accepts compute_dtype as a native torch.dtype or a string name (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64); MF mechanisms accept strategy-specific kwargs. |`
git show 873de427 -- docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md: the same substitution at line 138
docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70 - the contradicting rule, on the page the sibling removal 7f55aae5 rewrote

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:60-62 `_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_DTYPES = frozenset({torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64})` and :111-124 `_validate_compute_dtype` - accepts all four, no warning path
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1556-1584 `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` - maps the string names to torch dtypes, no warning

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:190-204 - `center_c = center.to(compute_dtype) if in_dtype != compute_dtype else center; sample = center_c + std * noise`, i.e. the clipped sum is downcast before noise is added
executed: TrainingArguments with {'compute_dtype':'bfloat16'} -> OK {'compute_dtype': torch.bfloat16}; 'float64' -> OK torch.float64; 'int8' -> ConfigurationError

measured worst realized norm on the clip sphere over 200 trials: bfloat16 1.0001227260086283 vs float32 1.0000001791386004 (C=1.0); noise value cardinality 2945 (bf16) vs 199721 (fp32) over 200000 samples at nm=1.0
findings.fix_sketch: Either restrict the DPTrainer surface to the dtypes precision.md endorses (float32/float64) and reject float16/bfloat16 in `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` with a message pointing at precision.md, or keep them and emit a one-time RuntimeWarning from `_validate_compute_dtype` whenever compute_dtype is narrower than float32, adding the precision.md caveat inline to docs/reference/transformers.md:196 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:138. Independently, stop downcasting the query: compute the noisy sum in the wider of `compute_dtype` and `center.dtype` so lowering compute_dtype cannot inflate the realized sensitivity above the accounted max_norm.

findings.title: Bounded-Gaussian removal left `bound` in the gaussian mechanism-kwargs allow-list, so the unknown-key error recommends the removed, privacy-unsound key
findings.claim: 873de427 (#1021) added an explicit guard rejecting `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound']` at _training_arguments.py:1222-1228 ("is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant") and stripped `bound` from the trainer's `_gn_extra` filter, but left `_MECHANISM_KWARGS["gaussian"] = frozenset({"bound", "compute_dtype"})` at :229 untouched. That set is the allow-list `_validate_privacy_kwargs` prints in its unknown-key error, so any typo in the gaussian mechanism kwargs produces an error message recommending the key the very next validator refuses - and naming a mechanism the library deliberately deleted because it has no matching accountant.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed: `TrainingArguments(output_dir=..., privacy_noise_multiplier=1.0, clipping_norm=1.0, privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bnd': 3.0})` raises `ConfigurationError: privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs contains unsupported keys for privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian': ['bnd']. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype'].` The user follows that advice, writes `{'bound': 3.0}`, and gets `ConfigurationError: privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant.` The stale entry is also the only remaining load-bearing reference to the removed mechanism in package source: if the explicit guard at :1222 is ever refactored away, `bound` becomes an accepted key again and is then silently dropped by the `_k == 'compute_dtype'` filter at _dp_trainer.py:1685 rather than rejected, so a user requesting bounded noise would get unbounded noise with no error.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:229 - `"gaussian": frozenset({"bound", "compute_dtype"}),` (untouched by 873de427, whose hunks in this file start at lines 150, 507, 1161 and 1553)
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:281-289 - `extra = set(kwargs) - allowed` ... `f"Allowed: {sorted(allowed) or '<none>'}."`

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1222-1228 - the `if "bound" in self.privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs: raise ConfigurationError(...)` guard added by the removal, which runs before the allow-list check at :1360-1365

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1678-1686 - `_gn_extra` keeps only `_k == "compute_dtype"`, so a surviving `bound` key would be dropped silently rather than raised

executed: `_MECHANISM_KWARGS['gaussian'] == ['bound', 'compute_dtype']`; both error messages reproduced verbatim; `bound` correctly rejected as a dict key, as a JSON string '{"bound": 3.0}', as an HF-style string 'bound=3.0', and under privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_identity'
findings.fix_sketch: Set `_MECHANISM_KWARGS["gaussian"] = frozenset({"compute_dtype"})` and keep the explicit `bound` guard purely as the migration message, or fold removed keys into a `_REMOVED_KWARGS` map consulted by `_validate_privacy_kwargs` so a removed key gets a targeted message instead of appearing in the 'Allowed' list.

clean_areas: Bounded-Gaussian removal (873de427) - surviving-reference sweep: `grep -rn -iE 'bounded_gaussian|bounded gaussian|BoundedGaussian|2211.17230|Chen and Hale|noise_bound'` across packages/, docs/, examples/, README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md returns zero hits (the only match in the tree is the audit's own .audit-checkpoint copy). The --noise-mechanism / --noise-bound CLI flags and their print/accounting branches are gone from examples/train_dpsgd.py, train_dpo.py and train_sft.py; docs/mechanisms/dp-sgd/gaussian.md, docs/user-guide/noise.md, docs/user-guide/dp-sgd.md, docs/reference/noise.md and docs/mechanisms/index.md no longer describe the variant; no .pyi, .rs, .toml, .ipynb or workflow file mentions it.

Bounded-Gaussian removal - API surface: `gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0), bound=3.0)` raises TypeError (pinned by packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py::test_bound_is_not_supported). The DPTrainer surface raises a targeted ConfigurationError for a `bound` key supplied as a dict, a JSON object string, or an HF-style 'bound=3.0' string, and under every mf_* mechanism (all four forms executed). Checked for false positives: `inspect.signature` over band_mf_strategy/blt_strategy/bisr_strategy/bsr_strategy/identity_strategy/lambda_cgd_strategy shows no factory takes a `bound` parameter, so the blanket guard cannot reject a legitimate MF config.

Bounded-Gaussian removal - checkpoint back-compat is fail-closed and the version ladder has no gap. `DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION` 7 -> 8 with `load_dp_runtime_state` raising `CheckpointError: unsupported dp_state bundle version N (expected 8)` (_checkpoint.py:399-404), covered by tests/opaque_transformers/test_checkpoint_helpers.py::test_rejects_pre_removal_bundle_version. Cross-checked the ladder against release tags by `git show <tag>:.../_checkpoint.py`: v0.15.0-v0.15.2 = 3, v0.15.3 = 4, v0.15.4 / v0.15.5.rc1 / v0.15.5.rc2 / v0.15.5 / v0.15.6.rc1 = 7, main = 8. Versions 5 and 6, and the transient version-7-before-#901 (which changed the MF noise-state layout without a bump), were never tagged, so no released checkpoint can be accepted against a mismatched runtime-state format.

Bounded-Gaussian removal - the replacement sampler is distributionally wider, not narrower, and the truncation pattern does not survive in siblings. `_sample` now calls `torch.randn(shape, dtype=compute_dtype, generator=generator)` instead of the old clamped inverse CDF (`center + std*sqrt(2)*erfinv(2u-1)` with u clamped to [eps, 1-eps]), which had truncated even the 'unbounded' path at about +/-5.1 sigma in float32 and +/-2.4 sigma in bfloat16. Measured 200000 draws per dtype at nm=1.0: mean about -4e-4, std about 1.0026, range +/-4.25 for float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 - no analytic clamp, and all four dtypes run without error. `grep -rn 'erfinv' packages/*/src` returns nothing; DP-FTRL's `_iid_normal_noise` (packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../noise/_engine.py:101-130) already used torch.randn; and `grep -rn 'clamp' ` over the dpsgd/dpftrl noise and noise_allocation modules shows no clamping of noise values anywhere.

Horizon-prefix removal (87404a1b) - the removed API is gone from every surface. `grep -rn -E 'per_step|PerStep|pld_at|horizon_pld_cache|prefix_pld'` over packages/, docs/ and examples/ returns only unrelated identifiers in optimizer/profiling test names. At runtime `hasattr(opaque.accounting, 'per_step') == False` and `hasattr(opaque.accounting.types, 'PerStep') == False`; `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip','gaussian','k_out_of_t','parallel_poisson','poisson']`; `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.__all__ == ['b_min_sep','balls_in_bins','mf_gaussian','poisson']`. On the Rust side `random_allocation_gaussian_prefix_pld` and `k_out_of_t_gaussian_prefix_pld` were removed consistently from amplification/mod.rs, python/amplification.rs, python/mod.rs and the .pyi stub, and `GeomPmf::add_constant` (used only by the prefix path) went with them. `ruff check packages/` passes, so no orphaned imports were left behind.

Horizon-prefix removal - legacy accountant state fails loud, not silent. Deserializing a pre-#894-shaped accountant JSON containing a `{"type": "PerStep", ...}` node through `opaque.serialization.from_state_dict(Accountant(), ...)` raises `CheckpointError: Unknown DpProcess type: PerStep` (executed). `CachedProcess` survives the round trip as `{"type": "CachedProcess", "inner": {...}}` and restores to the identical epsilon (0.245477285120814 before and after), so resuming a whole-horizon run does not lose the PLD cache boundary.

Horizon-prefix removal - full-horizon epsilon is numerically unchanged. Compared each surviving `pld()` line by line against the branch of the deleted `pld_at()` it replaced: `KOutOfT.pld` is exactly the old `n_steps == self.n_steps` branch (`epoch_pld(nm, self.n_steps, self.k, config)`); `BallsInBins.pld` substitutes `self.num_epochs == n_steps // num_bins`, `self.min_sep == num_bins`, `self.max_participations == num_epochs`, which are precisely the old `rounded == self.n_steps` values, including the BLT `toeplitz_gram_matrix(coefs, n_steps, min_sep, max_participations, False)` call and the Identity `sigma/sqrt(num_epochs)` reduction; `MfGaussian._pld_cache_key` only drops the `n_steps` override that prefix queries used. The nm==0 short-circuit was additionally hoisted ahead of the strategy dispatch in BallsInBins, widening non-private coverage from Identity-only to every strategy.

Horizon-prefix removal - the trainer's whole-horizon wiring is consistent and conservative. `_initialize_accounting` (_dp_trainer.py:275-282) installs `Accountant(prefix=acc.cached(process))` once and `_account_independent_step` no-ops because `ctx.step_process is None`, so the reported epsilon is the declared full-horizon bound from step 1 onward. Verified by isinstance that every amplifier the trainer can build is a DpHorizonProcess (CyclicPoisson, BMinSep, BallsInBins, KOutOfT -> True) while independently composed ones are not (Poisson, bare MfGaussian -> False), and that `build_amplifier_factory` has no branch returning a non-horizon process. The horizon is pinned to the training horizon (`_build_mechanism(..., n_steps=total_steps)` at :1619 plus the `int(_amp.n_steps) != total_steps` raise at :1695) and the loop cannot exceed it (`if global_step >= ctx.total_steps: break` at :2045 and :2069). Composition mistakes are conservative: composing KOutOfT twice gave 2.2749 vs 1.7894 once.

Horizon-prefix removal - privacy-based early stopping is disabled rather than left silently broken. TrainingArguments.__post_init__:1241-1257 raises when privacy_noise_multiplier and privacy_target_epsilon are both set for any mf_* mechanism or sampling_mode == 'k_out_of_t'; stop_at_step prediction and the in-loop epsilon fallback stop are both gated on `not ctx.is_horizon_process` (_dp_trainer.py:1218, 1248, 4219). docs/user-guide/accounting.md and docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md were rewritten to state that prefix queries and privacy-based early stopping are unsupported for these mechanisms; examples/train_dpftrl.py and examples/train_dpsgd.py now charge the horizon process once outside the loop and calibrate `mechanism(nm)` rather than `mechanism(nm) * total_steps`.

Horizon-prefix removal - resume is fail-closed on every horizon-relevant drift. `_validate_horizon_resume_calibration` (:5645-5680) rejects calibration-mode and target-epsilon drift before any state is restored; `_calibrate_noise` restores the saved multiplier for horizon resumes and raises on fixed-multiplier drift; RuntimeCheckpoint gained is_horizon_process / calibration_source / target_epsilon / horizon_process_state with compare_on_resume + dp_relevant metadata, and `_warn_on_arg_drift` upgrades total_steps' `intentional_extend` disposition to `dp_relevant` whenever either side is a horizon run, so k-out-of-t (which carries mechanism_kind='gaussian') cannot silently extend its horizon. `_apply_runtime_state`'s unconditional `ctx.accounting = accountant` was checked against this: for horizon runs the saved accountant is the same full-horizon process the fresh context would have built, and every field that could make them differ is drift-compared. 43/43 tests in test_dpftrl_trainer_smoke.py pass.

Horizon-prefix removal resolved OPQ-328 (#796) at the root rather than suppressing it: `cached()` no longer has the `_contains_horizon_process` warn-and-return branch (the whole helper was deleted). Measured on `Accountant(prefix=acc.cached(b_min_sep(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4)), n_steps=32, p0=0.01)))` under `warnings.simplefilter('always')`: zero warnings; first `epsilon_at(1e-5)` took 5.79 s (Monte Carlo), the second and third 0.000 s, all returning 1.0633 - the per-log-boundary MC re-evaluation that OPQ-328 described is genuinely amortized now, and the cache boundary survives serialization.

Horizon-prefix removal - the deleted `acc.nonprivate()` special case in the DP-FTRL branch of `_build_mechanism` is not needed. `MfGaussian.pld` short-circuits to `_native.non_private_pld` at noise_multiplier == 0, and executed `poisson/band_mf`, `b_min_sep/band_mf` and `balls_in_bins/identity` at nm=0 all return `epsilon_at(1e-5) == inf`, matching the documented noise_multiplier=0 behaviour.

Horizon-prefix removal - the native-signature change is consistent. `bandmf_b_min_sep_pld_from_transcript_handle` dropped its `n_steps` parameter; the single Python caller at packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_b_min_sep/__init__.py:188-194 passes the new 5-argument form, the .pyi stub at packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.pyi:455 matches, and the Rust `pld_from_transcript_handle` signature agrees.

Loss-scaling removal (7f55aae5) - no dangling references. `grep -rn -E 'all_finite|LossScaler|loss_scaler|unscale_grads|GradScaler'` over packages/, docs/ and examples/ returns only unrelated `torch.isfinite` assertions in optimizer/dpftrl tests plus the intentional `torch.amp.GradScaler` row in the precision.md compatibility table. `opaque.precision` / `opaque.api.engine.precision` were removed from AGENTS.md's package table and namespace list, from opaque-engine/pyproject.toml's `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] include`, and from .air/cloud/startup.sh's import smoke list; there is no docs/reference/precision.md and mkdocs.yml references only user-guide/precision.md. (The empty opaque/precision and opaque/api/engine/precision directories left in this working tree contain nothing but stale __pycache__ and are untracked by git, so a fresh clone or sdist does not ship them.)

Loss-scaling removal - the OPQ-333 (#807) sibling was fixed properly rather than deleted alongside its partner. `opaque.api.engine.pytree.global_norm` now raises `InputTypeError: ClippedPytree global norm is unsupported because global_norm() operates on raw tensor pytrees. Use .pytree for an explicit numerical-only view.` for ClippedPytree / NoisedPytree / SecondMomentClippingOutput / SecondMomentNoiseOutput (executed on a ClippedPytree) instead of silently returning tensor(0.); `unscale_grads`, the other half of OPQ-333, disappeared with the loss scaler.

Loss-scaling removal - the fp16 workflow it retired is closed off in code, not only in prose, and needed no checkpoint migration. `TrainingArguments.fp16` is a read-only property returning False (:1442-1444), `from_hf`'s REJECT_IF_SET refuses `fp16=True`, and `_setup_precision` only ever sets `_amp_dtype` to torch.bfloat16 or None. `LossScalerState` was never a field of RuntimeCheckpoint, so no bundle-version bump was required and none was made; a user who serialized one can no longer construct the template `from_state_dict` needs, which fails loudly at import. Clipping and noise still promote fp16/bf16 inputs to float32 by default (clipping compute_dtype=None; gaussian_noise and mf_gaussian_noise default torch.float32), matching precision.md's stated contract.

Regression run over the three removals' surviving code, with a freshly built opaque_accounting native module (the .so installed in the repo venv is stale and lacks the post-#850 `poisson_pld`, so an overlay build was used): `ruff check packages/` clean; 397 passed / 16 skipped in packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping + packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise; 210 passed in tests/opaque_transformers/test_config.py + test_checkpoint_helpers.py; 504 passed in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting + packages/opaque-accounting/tests; 43 passed in test_dpftrl_trainer_smoke.py - all under the PR marker expression `-m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed'`.

Bounded-Gaussian removal - test coverage was not thinned where it mattered. The 381-line test_bounded_gaussian.py was deleted, but the generic cases it also carried (returns_tuple, adds_noise_to_pytree, requires_clipped_input, rejects_already_noisy_input, dtype/device preservation, nested/tuple pytree, reproducibility, invalid key type, per-group noise) all have live equivalents among the 30 tests in packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py, and the commit added test_bound_is_not_supported plus parameterised supported/rejected compute_dtype tests in test_gaussian_compute_dtype.py.
